newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine trade deficit widens to record high.
newsitem.headline: Philippine trade deficit widens to record high.

text.p: The Philippine government said on Friday that trade deficit widened to record levels in November, but analysts said this was not alarming and was to be expected in a fast-growing economy.
The National Statistics Office (NSO) said the merchandise trade deficit in the first eleven months of 1996 reached $10.951 billion against $8.141 billion in the same 1995 period.
The record for a full calendar-year trade deficit was $9.091 billion in 1995.
"It should not be a cause for concern, since the rest of the economy is doing very well," Noel Reyes, research head of Anscor Hagedorn, said.
"We need a lot of things that are not easily available in the country, such as capital equipment and even new technologies."
Analysts said most of the imports were capital equipment and raw materials integral to a growing economy.
The Philippine economy has been growing at a sustained pace since 1993 with gross national product (GNP) in 1996 expected to grow by more than 7.0 percent.
"We should not look at the trade deficit in isolation. We should look at the current account situation," said Luz Lorenzo, chief economist of Peregrine Securities.
The country's current account has been in surplus due to an influx of foreign portfolio capital and remittances of overseas Filipino workers.
